title: Checks for arguments to == which have their address taken to satisfy a bound and suggests to dereference the other argument instead
summary: It is more idiomatic to dereference the other argument. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of .as_ref().cloned() and .as_mut().cloned() on Options
summary: This can be written more concisely by cloning the Option directly. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of _.as_ref().map(Deref::deref) or its aliases (such as String::as_str).
summary: Readability, this can be written more concisely as _.as_deref(). Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of option_env!(...).unwrap() and suggests usage of the env! macro.
summary: Unwrapping the result of option_env! will panic at run-time if the environment variable doesn’t exist, whereas env! catches it at compile-time. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for iterators of Options using .filter(Option::is_some).map(Option::unwrap) that may be replaced with a .flatten() call.
summary: Option is like a collection of 0-1 things, so flatten automatically does this without suspicious-looking unwrap calls. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Lints usage of if let Some(v) = ... { y } else { x } and match .. { Some(v) => y, None/_ => x } which are more idiomatically done with Option::map_or (if the else bit is a pure expression) or Option::map_or_else (if the else bit is an impure expression).
summary: Using the dedicated functions of the Option type is clearer and more concise than an if let expression. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for usage of _.map_or(None, _).
summary: Readability, this can be written more concisely as _.and_then(_). Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of option.map(f) where f is a function or closure that returns the unit type ().
summary: Readability, this can be written more clearly with an if let statement Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of Option<Option<_>> in function signatures and type definitions
summary: Option<_> represents an optional value. Option<Option<_>> represents an optional value which itself wraps an optional. This is logically the same thing as an optional value but has an unneeded extra level of wrapping. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
